Treat the range as this curator's guidance, and state only observations supported by the supplied evidence.

analyses.content: The catalog's early 180–200-word label guidance was explicitly unconfirmed. The fictional curator later requested 35–50 words after approving a 42-word draft containing one clear observation (Trial A). Routine visitor observation says visitors read the first sentence and large-print species name and usually skip the provenance appendix. These sources support prioritizing concise, readable display text for this exhibit, while the visitor observation alone does not establish a preferred word count. Trial B reports a 190-word label went unread because it did not fit the display. Trial C reports a short label failed because it claimed a wild pollinator unsupported by observations. Together these outcomes support checking both physical fit and factual support; length alone is insufficient. The supplied specimen facts establish that flowers opened after sunset and closed the next morning in an indoor trial, with three of twelve buds opening; they do not establish a wild pollinator. No delivered later Work outcome is present, so these are source-reported trials, not feedback on changes made in this Work. This is a bounded review of the enumerated materials; it does not establish coverage of later arrivals or other unexamined material.
